task.title: Rotating a legacy OAuth 2 access token
task.shortdesc: To replace a legacy long-lived OAuth 2 access token, you can create a named token with an explicit expiration policy and then revoke the legacy token.

ul.li: You have an organization OAuth application that already has a legacy token.
You can update any CI system, script, or client that currently uses the legacy token.

context.p: Existing legacy tokens continue to work for at least 10 years until you revoke them.

step.cmd: On the Red Hat Quay UI, click Organization → OAuth Applications.
Identify the legacy token to replace. Legacy tokens do not have a user-defined name, do not show a creation date, and have an expiration date of 10 years from the date of creation.

substep.cmd: Set an expiration appropriate for the workload, for example 7 days or 10 years.
Select the scopes required by the client.

step.cmd: Click Generate Token, then click Authorize Application and confirm the authorization.
Copy the new token secret and store it securely.
Update the CI system, script, or client configuration to use the new token.
Verify that the client works with the new token.
Return to the OAuth Applications page and revoke the legacy token:

substep.cmd: Click the application name that owns the legacy token.
Click the menu kebab icon for the legacy token.
Click Revoke. Confirm that you want to revoke the token by clicking Revoke token.
